name: United States
note: Shown with 50 stars; the 1945 flag had 48.

name: United Kingdom
historicalName: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

name: Soviet Union
politicalStatus: Independent union of republics, victorious Allied power
note: The Soviet flag was a red field bearing a gold hammer-and-sickle beneath a red star outlined in gold. This is a deliberately simplified rendering (a single gold mark standing in for the hammer-and-sickle emblem, which could not be reproduced accurately here) — not a claim of the exact historical design.

name: France (Provisional Government)
historicalName: Gouvernement provisoire de la République française
politicalStatus: Provisional government, pending the Fourth Republic (1946)
note: The tricolor, unchanged since 1830, continued under the postwar provisional government.

name: Republic of China
note: The Nationalist government's "Blue Sky, White Sun, Wholly Red Earth" flag, adopted 1928, was the Republic of China's flag in 1945 — this is the same design still used by Taiwan today, since the government later relocated there in 1949 after the Chinese Civil War.

name: Japan
note: The Hinomaru remained Japan's flag through defeat and the start of Allied occupation, though its public display was restricted by occupation authorities for a period afterward.

name: Kingdom of Italy
politicalStatus: Kingdom in transition (monarchy abolished by referendum the following year, 1946)
note: The Kingdom of Italy technically continued until the 1946 referendum that created the Republic; the House of Savoy arms had already been dropped from common civilian use by 1945, matching today's plain tricolor.

name: Poland
politicalStatus: Reconstituted state under a Soviet-backed provisional government (contested by the London government-in-exile)
note: Poland's borders shifted substantially westward at the war's end. The white-red bicolor continued in use; political legitimacy was contested between the Soviet-backed provisional government in Warsaw and the Polish government-in-exile in London.

name: Democratic Republic of Vietnam
historicalName: Việt Nam Dân chủ Cộng hòa
politicalStatus: Declared independence Sept 2, 1945; not yet recognized by France
note: Ho Chi Minh declared independence September 2, 1945; the red flag with a central yellow star was confirmed as the new state's flag within days. France did not recognize the declaration, and the First Indochina War followed.

name: Republic of Indonesia
politicalStatus: Declared independence Aug 17, 1945; not yet recognized by the Netherlands
note: Sukarno declared independence August 17, 1945, adopting the red-white bicolor still used today. The Netherlands did not recognize the declaration until 1949, after the Indonesian National Revolution.
